elements.element: Customer may assign without Vendor consent to an affiliate
elements.evidence: Company may assign this Agreement ... without Contractor's consent to an affiliate of Company

elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets
elements.evidence: or to a successor in connection with a merger, acquisition, reorganization or sale of all or substantially all of its assets

elements.element: Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent, not to be unreasonably withheld
elements.evidence: Neither party shall assign ... without the other party's express, prior written consent, which will not be unreasonably withheld

elements.element: Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor
elements.evidence: Contractor shall not assign or transfer this Agreement to any competitor of Company

elements.element: No Vendor termination right on Customer's change of control
elements.evidence: No change of control of Company shall ... entitle Contractor to terminate ... this Agreement

elements.element: Mutual right to assign to successors with written notice
elements.evidence: upon written notice to Contractor; Neither party shall assign ... without the other party's ... consent

elements.element: Consent for other assignments not unreasonably withheld
elements.evidence: which will not be unreasonably withheld

offending_extra_words: or business to which this Agreement relates
No change of control of Company shall constitute an assignment requiring consent
reasons: All preferred atomic elements are satisfied: Customer affiliate and successor carve-out, Vendor consent standard preserved, competitor bar on Vendor, and no Vendor termination right on Customer change of control.
Minimality fails: the operation replaces 14 words with 109 words (ratio 7.79) and changes 86% of characters, where a short proviso plus one sentence would suffice.

Extra scope beyond the locked preferred level: 'in whole or in part', 'reorganization', 'or business to which this Agreement relates', the deemed-non-assignment rule, and the added 'suspend or re-price' and Statement of Work reference duplicate/expand protection not required by the position.
'upon written notice to Contractor' imports a fallback mechanic and attaches a condition to our own consent-free assignment right; it is unnecessary at the preferred level.
Intent preserved: the original mutual consent-not-unreasonably-withheld standard and subcontracting restriction remain effective and no undefined term or contradiction is introduced.
